# ggthemes <a href="https://jrnold.github.io/ggthemes/"><img src="man/figures/stickers/ggthemes-theme-stickers.gif" align="right" height="139" alt="Animated ggthemes hex stickers, cycling through stickers drawn in the package's themes" /></a>

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/jrnold/ggthemes/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jrnold/ggthemes/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Code Coverage Status](https://codecov.io/gh/jrnold/ggthemes/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/github/jrnold/ggthemes?branch=main)
[![CRAN downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/ggthemes)](https://www.r-pkg.org/pkg/ggthemes)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/ggthemes)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggthemes)
[![lifecycle](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-stable-brightgreen.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#stable)

ggthemes adds themes, scales and geoms to [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/)
that reproduce the look of well-known publications and software, and of the
graphics advocated by Edward Tufte and Stephen Few:

- **Themes** after *The Economist*, *The Wall Street Journal*, FiveThirtyEight,
  Excel, LibreOffice Calc, Google Docs, Highcharts, Apple Numbers, Stata,
  Solarized, base R graphics and more.
- **Color, shape and linetype scales and palettes** to match, including
  colorblind-safe and Tableau palettes. See the
  [palette gallery](https://jrnold.github.io/ggthemes/articles/palettes.html).
- **Geoms** for Tufte's range frames and minimal box plots, and tools for
  [banking to 45°](https://jrnold.github.io/ggthemes/reference/bank_slopes.html)
  to choose a plot's aspect ratio.

```{r hero, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6.2, out.width = "100%", fig.alt = "The same scatter plot of fuel economy against car weight drawn four ways: with theme_economist(), theme_fivethirtyeight(), theme_wsj() and theme_solarized(), each with its matching color scale."}
library("ggplot2")
library("ggthemes")

hero_data <- within(mtcars, gear <- factor(gear))
hero_base <- ggplot(hero_data, aes(wt, mpg, colour = gear)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Miles per gallon", colour = "Gears")
hero <- list(
  hero_base + theme_economist() + scale_colour_economist() + labs(title = "theme_economist()"),
  hero_base + theme_fivethirtyeight() + scale_colour_fivethirtyeight() + labs(title = "theme_fivethirtyeight()"),
  hero_base + theme_wsj(base_size = 9) + scale_colour_wsj() + labs(title = "theme_wsj()"),
  hero_base + theme_solarized() + scale_colour_solarized() + labs(title = "theme_solarized()")
)
grid::grid.newpage()
grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(2, 2)))
for (i in seq_along(hero)) {
  print(hero[[i]], vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = (i - 1) %/% 2 + 1, layout.pos.col = (i - 1) %% 2 + 1))
}
```

## Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

```r
install.packages("ggthemes")
```

Or the development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jrnold/ggthemes")
```

## Themes

Every theme is shown below with its matching color scale, where it has one.
Each figure links to the theme's reference page.

<details>
<summary>Data and base plots used in the examples</summary>

```{r setup-examples}
library("ggplot2")
library("ggthemes")

mtcars2 <- within(mtcars, {
  vs <- factor(vs, labels = c("V-shaped", "Straight"))
  am <- factor(am, labels = c("Automatic", "Manual"))
  cyl  <- factor(cyl)
  gear <- factor(gear)
})

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = gear)) +
  labs(
    title = "Fuel economy falls with weight",
    x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
    y = "Fuel economy (mpg)",
    colour = "Gears"
  )

# `theme_map()` intentionally removes axes, so use geographic data rather than
# a scatterplot. `theme_solid()` is likewise intended to leave only geoms.
us_states <- map_data("state")
p_map <- ggplot(us_states, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
  geom_polygon(aes(fill = region), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
  coord_map("albers", lat0 = 39, lat1 = 45) +
  guides(fill = "none")

p_solid <- ggplot(mtcars2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = gear), size = 3) +
  guides(colour = "none")
```

</details>

```{r examples, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# One cell per exported theme, alphabetically. Each entry is the literal code
# shown under the figure *and* the code evaluated to draw it, so the two
# cannot drift apart. Themes that ship their own palette are paired with it;
# the rest borrow a general-purpose one.
examples <- list(
  theme_base = "p1 + theme_base() +\n  scale_colour_colourblind()",
  theme_calc = "p1 + theme_calc() +\n  scale_colour_calc()",
  theme_clean = "p1 + theme_clean() +\n  scale_colour_tableau()",
  theme_economist = "p1 + theme_economist() +\n  scale_colour_economist()",
  theme_excel = "p1 + theme_excel() +\n  scale_colour_excel()",
  theme_excel_new = "p1 + theme_excel_new() +\n  scale_colour_excel_new()",
  theme_few = "p1 + theme_few() +\n  scale_colour_few()",
  theme_fivethirtyeight = "p1 + theme_fivethirtyeight() +\n  scale_colour_fivethirtyeight()",
  theme_foundation = "p1 + theme_foundation() +\n  scale_colour_colourblind()",
  theme_gdocs = "p1 + theme_gdocs() +\n  scale_colour_gdocs()",
  theme_hc = "p1 + theme_hc() +\n  scale_colour_hc()",
  theme_igray = "p1 + theme_igray()",
  theme_map = "p_map +\n  theme_map()",
  theme_numbers = "p1 + theme_numbers() +\n  scale_colour_numbers()",
  theme_pander = "p1 + theme_pander() +\n  scale_colour_pander()",
  theme_par = "p1 + theme_par() +\n  scale_colour_colourblind()",
  theme_solarized = "p1 + theme_solarized() +\n  scale_colour_solarized()",
  theme_solarized_2 = "p1 + theme_solarized_2() +\n  scale_colour_solarized()",
  theme_solid = "p_solid +\n  theme_solid(fill = \"#202124\") +\n  scale_colour_tableau()",
  theme_stata = "p1 + theme_stata() +\n  scale_colour_stata()",
  theme_tufte = "p1 + theme_tufte() +\n  scale_colour_few()",
  theme_wsj = "p1 + theme_wsj(base_size = 8) +\n  scale_colour_wsj()"
)

# Link each figure to the pkgdown reference page of the Rd file documenting it.
rd_files <- list.files("man", pattern = "[.]Rd$", full.names = TRUE)
rd_page <- unlist(lapply(rd_files, function(f) {
  aliases <- regmatches(readLines(f), regexpr("(?<=^\\\\alias\\{)[^}]+", readLines(f), perl = TRUE))
  setNames(rep(sub("[.]Rd$", "", basename(f)), length(aliases)), aliases)
}))
reference_url <- function(fn) {
  sprintf("https://jrnold.github.io/ggthemes/reference/%s.html", rd_page[[fn]])
}

cell <- function(nm) {
  code <- examples[[nm]]
  path <- paste0("man/figures/README-", nm, "-1.png")
  # A white background keeps themes that draw none (theme_map(), theme_tufte())
  # legible on dark-mode pages.
  ggsave(path, plot = eval(parse(text = code)), width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 96, bg = "white")
  sprintf(
    "<td valign=\"top\" width=\"50%%\">\n<a href=\"%s\"><img src=\"%s\" width=\"100%%\" alt=\"Example plot drawn with %s()\"></a>\n\n```r\n%s\n```\n\n</td>\n",
    reference_url(nm), path, nm, code
  )
}

cat("<table>\n")
for (pair in split(names(examples), ceiling(seq_along(examples) / 2))) {
  cat("<tr>\n", vapply(pair, cell, character(1)), "</tr>\n", sep = "")
}
cat("</table>\n")
```

## Color palettes

A sample of the color palettes is shown below. The
[palette gallery](https://jrnold.github.io/ggthemes/articles/palettes.html)
shows every palette in the package.

```{r palette-sample, include = FALSE}
# Defined in its own chunk: the figure size below is computed from it, and
# knitr evaluates chunk options before the chunk's code.
source("vignettes/articles/swatches.R")
palette_sample <- list(
  "colorblind_pal()" = colorblind_pal()(8),
  "economist_pal()" = economist_pal()(9),
  "fivethirtyeight_pal()" = fivethirtyeight_pal()(3),
  'few_pal("Medium")' = few_pal("Medium")(8),
  "solarized_pal()" = solarized_pal()(8),
  'stata_pal("s2color")' = stata_pal("s2color")(15),
  'tableau_color_pal("Tableau 10")' = tableau_color_pal("Tableau 10")(10),
  'wsj_pal("colors6")' = wsj_pal("colors6")(6)
)
```

```{r palettes, echo = FALSE, dpi = 144, fig.width = swatch_width(palette_sample), fig.height = swatch_height(palette_sample), fig.alt = "Swatches of eight palettes: colorblind, Economist, FiveThirtyEight, Few, Solarized, Stata, Tableau 10 and Wall Street Journal."}
swatch_plot(palette_sample)
```

## Geoms

`geom_rangeframe()` draws Tufte's range frame, axis lines that span only the
range of the data. `geom_tufteboxplot()` draws his minimal box plot.

```{r geoms, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.5, out.width = "49%", fig.show = "hold", fig.alt = c("Scatter plot of fuel economy against weight with theme_tufte(), whose axis lines span only the range of the data.", "Tufte-style box plots of fuel economy by number of cylinders: a point for the median and lines for the whiskers.")}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_rangeframe() +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Miles per gallon") +
  theme_tufte()

ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg)) +
  geom_tufteboxplot() +
  labs(x = "Cylinders", y = "Miles per gallon") +
  theme_tufte()
```
